scope: Node VM regression tests plus automated real-browser E2E (playwright, headless Chromium)
fixedInThisVersion: Established by a non-browser test (PowerShell + curl.exe, tools/probe-jev.ps1) that api.typesafe.ai answers correctly but sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin. A browser cannot read the response, so the direct route can never work from a page. The earlier header hypothesis was wrong and is now closed.

Added a jev-extension route that carries the same request through the add-on background, which is not subject to CORS for hosts the user has granted. The request body and headers are asserted byte-identical to jev-direct so the two cannot drift.

Added extension/turn-proxy.js: a relay restricted to one user-approved https origin, an explicit header allowlist, a 256KB request / 1MB reply / 30s cap, and senders limited to the add-on pages and the registered HTML tab. It is not a general-purpose fetch proxy.

Added a popup row that requests the host permission for the decision-layer origin and reports stored-versus-granted separately, so a revoked permission is visible rather than surfacing as a network error.
Relayed HTTP errors keep their status, so NEVER_RETRY (401/404 stops the layer) still fires through the relay.
Unreachable is now split into needsBridge, needsSetup and CORS, because reporting all three as CORS sends the user to the wrong fix.
reviewNotReproduced: Carried over from v1.4.13: the external review reported double counting of a single response. Still not reproduced; committedBySource increments once per commit and correctedBySource once per correction.
regressionProof: Two deliberate mutations were applied to app.js and both were caught: falling back to a direct fetch when the relay is unavailable failed "it must fail rather than send", and dropping the relayed status failed "401 through the relay must still stop the layer". The file was restored from a checksum-verified copy afterwards.
realBrowserE2E: tests/test-browser.cjs and tests/test-settings-ui.cjs both pass; the settings E2E now also asserts the add-on route appears in the real picker.
notVerified: Any successful Jev round trip through the relay. The relay is covered by unit tests against a stubbed worker and a stubbed fetch; no real response from api.typesafe.ai has yet been parsed in a browser. That remains the completion criterion before thresholds or question wording are touched.
Tokyo-to-api.typesafe.ai latency, and whether the 1,200 req/min account-wide cap is workable for concurrent meetings.
